info.name: smart-subtitle-converter-api
info.description:
Every smart-subtitle-converter-api endpoint with the README examples, plus negative cases.

Set `baseUrl` (default http://localhost:8080) and `apiKey` in the environment. A key is required by default: use the key the API generated into its api_keys.txt on first start (read it from the file; it is never logged), or one of your own. Leave apiKey empty only for a server started with API_AUTH_DISABLED=true. File parts use paths relative to the repository root: in Postman set Settings -> General -> Working directory to your checkout; with newman pass `--working-dir <checkout>`.

Every request sends `Authorization: Bearer {{apiKey}}` when apiKey is set, except those tagged [no auth].

Storage/job examples: URI transfers are opt-in. Fill fileInput/fileOutput, s3Input/s3Output, or httpsInput/httpsOutput only for storage you have configured. fileOutput is a complete-file template; each write inserts a GUID to avoid replacing files. Leave unused values empty to skip. Never commit signed URLs or credentials.

Job file routes re-read stored input/output, not cached bytes; ids are capability tokens for any valid API key. ifExists is error (default) | replace. Disk/S3 default to collision errors; presigned HTTPS PUT follows signer/receiver policy. S3 output values are complete-key templates with a fresh GUID per example.

request.description: Liveness probe. Always open, even with API keys on.
Readiness: startup self-test (SRT->WebVTT), Skia, ICU/globalization probes, worker, queue. 503 + `failing` when not ready.

exec: pm.test("all checks ok", () => Object.entries(j.checks).forEach(([k, v]) => pm.expect(v, k).to.eql("ok")));

request.description: Every libse format with id, aliases, extensions and capabilities.
Filter by id/name/alias/extension.
Built-in + mounted presets. Invalid mounted files are listed with their errors (troubleshoot mounts here).
Raw JSON and resolved profile (extends flattened).
Always 200 for a JSON object; `valid`, `errors`, `warnings`, `resolved`.
Errors carry a JSON pointer and a hint.
JSON Schema 2020-12 for profiles (editors, agents).
`kind` (text, binary, image, container; comma list) and `writable=true` filters.

exec: pm.test("EBU STL, PAC, Cavena 890 writable", () => ["ebustl", "pacscreenelectronics", "cavena890"].forEach(i => pm.expect(ids).to.include(i)));

request.description: What is this file? Format, encoding, language, cue count, candidates.
Binary input: kind, codePage (the GSI CPN) and formatDetails.

item.name: Detect: BOM, line endings, source warnings

request.description: Since 1.2.0 detect reports bom and lineEndings for text input, and warnings for zero-length cues and U+FFFD already in the source.
Simplest call: a file and a target format id or alias.

formdata.description: Default error | explicit replace; applies when output is supplied.

request.description: A built-in preset by name.
Overrides merge onto the preset: objects merge, arrays replace, null clears.
A full profile in the `profile` part, no preset.
Legacy encodings are detected and reported in X-Detected-Encoding.
For agents and scripts: content inline (text or base64), outputs inline.
Binary target with GSI options. Output is application/octet-stream; lossy steps are warnings (characters-replaced, frame-quantised).

An STL30.01 file whose cues are 29.97 fps (readFrameRate), rewritten with defaults (the source GSI is reused). EBU Tech 3264 has no 29.97 code, so the output still says STL30.01 and the API warns frame-rate-changed. Fix: formatOptions.ebuStl.frameRate (e.g. 30) or headerFromSource:false.
Detected by content; X-Detected-Code-Page is the GSI code page.
PAC code-page auto-detection is weak for non-Latin scripts: name the source format and the input code page.
Binary content must be base64 (contentEncoding).
Binary outputs are always base64, whatever responseEncoding says.

item.name: JSON: Greek SRT -> PAC (verification, remedy hint)

request.description: Every binary output is read back (outputs[].verification, since 1.2.0). Greek doesn't fit the default PAC latin code page: verdict lossy, characters-replaced with cue numbers, code points and a hint (formatOptions.pac.codePage=greek or target fpc). Nothing is switched automatically.

exec: const j = pm.response.json(); const v = j.outputs[0].verification;
pm.test("verdict lossy, 2 cues written and read back", () => { pm.expect(v.verdict).to.eql("lossy"); pm.expect(v.cuesWritten).to.eql(2); pm.expect(v.cuesReadBack).to.eql(2); });
pm.test("replacedChars lists cues and Greek code points", () => { pm.expect(v.replacedChars.cues).to.eql([1, 2]); pm.expect(v.replacedChars.codePoints[0].codePoint).to.match(/^U\+03/); });
pm.test("warning has details and a remedy hint", () => { pm.expect(w.details.cues).to.eql([1, 2]); pm.expect(w.hint).to.include("greek"); pm.expect(w.hint).to.include("fpc"); });

pm.test("remedy facts (1.2.1)", () => { const r = w.details.remedy; pm.expect(r.option).to.eql("formatOptions.pac.codePage"); pm.expect(r.allowedValues).to.include("greek"); pm.expect(r.suggested).to.eql("greek"); pm.expect(r.candidatesTested).to.eql(true); pm.expect(r.unicodeAlternative).to.eql("fpc"); });

item.name: JSON: zero-length cue -> EBU STL (clear warning)

request.description: A zero-length cue (often metadata) can't be stored in EBU STL: it reads back as 99:59:59,999. zero-length-cue names the source cue; lossy-format says what happened and how to fix it (ApplyDurationLimits, or remove the cue). A fresh EBU header also gets format-defaults-applied (No Title / USA / language) because no formatOptions.ebuStl fields were set.

exec: pm.test("lossy-format names the cue and 99:59:59,999", () => { pm.expect(l.message).to.include("zero-length cue(s) 1"); pm.expect(l.message).to.include("99:59:59,999"); });

pm.test("format-defaults-applied lists the header fields libse filled in", () => { const f = j.warnings.find(x => x.code === "format-defaults-applied").details.fields; pm.expect(f.originalProgrammeTitle).to.eql("No Title"); pm.expect(f.countryOfOrigin).to.eql("USA"); });

request.description: PAC and PAC Unicode (FPC) share their header; the .fpc file name decides.
Image-based formats (e.g. Blu-ray SUP) need OCR: 422 format-not-supported.
Validation errors point at the field and suggest a fix.
/v1/convert takes multipart/form-data; JSON goes to /v1/convert/json.
With API keys on, /v1 needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Skipped when the environment has no apiKey (open server).

if (!pm.environment.get("apiKey")) { pm.test.skip("wrong key -> 401 (no apiKey set)", () => {}); return; }

request.description: Readable but not writable here: 422 format-not-writable; the hint points at ?writable=true.

item.name: JSON: text content for a binary source

request.description: Binary content must be base64: 422 invalid-binary-input, pointer /contentEncoding.
Well-formed but not allowed: 400 format-option-invalid.
/v1/convert/json takes application/json: 415.
Since 1.2.0: bytes valid as both PAC and PAC Unicode, with no deciding file name, are rejected (422 ambiguous-format, candidates) instead of guessed. Set profile.source.format to pac or fpc.

A request whose Origin header names a host that is not in ALLOWED_HOSTS is refused before auth, so a web page can't use the API from someone's browser. Requests without Origin (curl, scripts, the MCP) are not affected.
